text: Using a modified telomeric repeat amplification protocol (TRAP), telomerase activity was detected in crickets, cockroaches, and two Lepidopteran insects, despite insect telomeres generally comprising pentanucleotide (TTAGG)n repeats—absent in Diptera and some species that may maintain telomeres without telomerase. Cricket and cockroach telomerase required dATP, dGTP, and dTTP, but not dCTP; sequence analyses confirmed (TTAGG)n repeats are synthesized by telomerase. Cockroach telomerase occurred in somatic cells (fat body, muscle, neural tissue) and germ line (testis), showing non-tissue-specific expression in adults. High activity appeared in crickets and cockroaches, but none in Bombyx mori tissues or cultures, nor in two Drosophila and one Sarcophaga cell line—supporting the theory that Dipteran insects maintain telomeres without telomerase.
